# BLO-32734 — decouple the pod-log unlink from the Job delete

[#1724](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1724) ·
[BLO-32734](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-32734) AC2 ·
`src/server/execute.ts`, `src/server/execute.test.ts`

Stopped `cleanupJob` gating the pod-log `fs.unlink` on `deleteNamespacedJob`
succeeding. Both steps sat in one `try`, so every Job-delete failure — routinely
a 404, because the Job is often already gone via `ttlSecondsAfterFinished`, an
external delete, or a prior reattach — threw past the unlink into a `catch` that
named the Job and never the file; ≥20,480 orphaned `.pod.ndjson` accumulated
silently on the shared volume.

The unlink now runs regardless of the Job-delete outcome; `ENOENT` stays silent
(the pod may never have written a log) and any other unlink failure is warned.
The Job-delete failure is still reported — the two steps are decoupled, not the
first silenced. `skipCleanup`/`retainJobs` still retain the log by design.

`warnQuietly` fixes a latent bug wider than the stated scope: the old
`await onLog(...)` in the Job-delete `catch` could itself reject out of
`cleanupJob`, and the dominant call site is a `finally`, so a dead log sink
would have masked the block's real outcome. It swallows a non-promise return as
well as a rejection.

`cleanupJob` and `reapPodLogFile` are exported for direct testing. Seven cases
cover Job-delete success, a 404, another delete failure, a silent `ENOENT`, an
undefined `podLogPath`, and `onLog` rejecting while reporting either the
Job-delete failure or the unlink failure. The 404 case is a verified falsifier —
it reddens if the unlink is moved back inside the Job-delete `try` — and it also
asserts the Job-delete warning is still emitted, pinning "decouple, don't
silence" rather than just the happy path. The non-`ENOENT` warn path is driven
by pointing `unlink` at a directory rather than by mocking `node:fs`, so it
exercises the real syscall.

Does not reduce the existing backlog, and does not cover runs that die before
reaching `cleanupJob` (pod OOM, node eviction, `BackoffLimitExceeded`) — that
class needs a sweeper, per the AC2 scope note on the issue.

## Why this is an entry file and not a row in PROVENANCE-CHANGES.md

This change originally appended its row to the frozen
[PROVENANCE-CHANGES.md](../PROVENANCE-CHANGES.md); the guard accepts that with a
warning. It is moved here instead because that file is exactly what ejects a PR
from the merge queue — [#2070](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2070),
[#1459](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1459) and
[#1699](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1699) (three times) all went
`DIRTY` on a conflict in that one file and nothing else. An ejection forces a
rebase and re-push, which voids the at-head review attestation. Relative to this
PR's base the row did not exist, so moving it removes no record.
